question:
Intracellular iron homeostasis is increasingly recognized as a regulator of cancer cell behavior, but how iron distribution influences extracellular matrix (ECM) organization and invasion remains poorly understood.

Three candidate results follow. Exactly one is what this study reported.
- Result A: Here, we show that loss of divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1/SLC11A2) disrupts intracellular iron homeostasis and promotes cancer cell invasion through an iron-ER-ECM axis. In MDA-MB-231 cells, DMT1 knockout (KO) reduced total iron content but increased the labile iron pool (LIP) in both 2D and 3D culture models, indicating altered intracellular iron distribution. Across transcriptomic and phenotypic readouts, DMT1-dependent effects were more evident in 3D than in 2D models, with DMT1 KO inducing endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and impaired collagen/ECM organization. Functionally, the DMT1-loss phenotype was marked by reduced 2D motility, whereas in 3D spheroid models DMT1 KO cells displayed enhanced invasive outgrowth in both Matrigel and collagen matrices. Iron chelation further modulated this phenotype in a DMT1-dependent manner. Pharmacologic induction of ER stress phenocopied the loose spheroid architecture and invasive behavior, supporting ER stress as a mechanistic link between altered iron handling and ECM destabilization. Together, these findings identify intracellular iron distribution, rather than total iron abundance alone, as a determinant of ECM integrity and context-dependent cancer cell invasion. One Sentence Summary: Iron misrouting, not iron excess, drives ER stress and collagen failure that unleash invasion in triple-negative breast cancer.
- Result B: Here, we show that loss of divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1/SLC11A2) disrupts intracellular iron homeostasis and promotes cancer cell invasion through an iron-mitochondrial-ECM axis. In MDA-MB-231 cells, DMT1 knockout (KO) reduced total iron content but increased the labile iron pool (LIP) in both 2D and 3D culture models, indicating altered intracellular iron distribution. Across transcriptomic and phenotypic readouts, DMT1-dependent effects were more evident in 3D than in 2D models, with DMT1 KO inducing mitochondrial stress and impaired collagen/ECM organization. Functionally, the DMT1-loss phenotype was marked by reduced 2D motility, whereas in 3D spheroid models DMT1 KO cells displayed enhanced invasive outgrowth in both Matrigel and collagen matrices. Iron chelation further modulated this phenotype in a DMT1-dependent manner. Pharmacologic induction of mitochondrial stress phenocopied the loose spheroid architecture and invasive behavior, supporting mitochondrial stress as a mechanistic link between altered iron handling and ECM destabilization. Together, these findings identify intracellular iron distribution, rather than total iron abundance alone, as a determinant of ECM integrity and context-dependent cancer cell invasion. One Sentence Summary: Iron misrouting, not iron excess, drives mitochondrial stress and collagen failure that unleash invasion in triple-negative breast cancer.
- Result C: Here, we show that loss of divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1/SLC11A2) disrupts intracellular iron homeostasis and suppresses cancer cell invasion through an iron-ER-ECM axis. In MDA-MB-231 cells, DMT1 knockout (KO) increased total iron content but reduced the labile iron pool (LIP) in both 2D and 3D culture models, indicating altered intracellular iron distribution. Across transcriptomic and phenotypic readouts, DMT1-dependent effects were more evident in 3D than in 2D models, with DMT1 KO alleviating endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and promoting collagen/ECM organization. Functionally, the DMT1-loss phenotype was marked by increased 2D motility, whereas in 3D spheroid models DMT1 KO cells displayed reduced invasive outgrowth in both Matrigel and collagen matrices. Iron chelation further modulated this phenotype in a DMT1-dependent manner. Pharmacologic inhibition of ER stress phenocopied the compact spheroid architecture and reduced invasive behavior, supporting ER stress as a mechanistic link between altered iron handling and ECM stabilization. Together, these findings identify intracellular iron distribution, rather than total iron abundance alone, as a determinant of ECM integrity and context-dependent cancer cell invasion. One Sentence Summary: Iron retention, not misrouting, sustains ER homeostasis and collagen integrity that restrain invasion in triple-negative breast cancer.
Which result did this study report? Rank the candidates, and give the mechanism, the key evidence, and a validation experiment for the top pick.
